chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left his wife while she was pregnant, so she gave birth to a boy after his death. Then the boy died after falling onto the ground. The midwife who received him testified that he cried out and shrieked when he fell onto the ground, then died after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon the Imam to validate her testimony regarding one-quarter of the inheritance of the boy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a newborn's inheritance if they die immediately after birth and only the midwife testifies?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the evidentiary standard for establishing a newborn's viability (istihlal) through the midwife's testimony of a cry upon birth, a crucial prerequisite for inheritance rights in Shia jurisprudence. It specifically grants the mother one-quarter of the infant's estate, reflecting the principle that the child is considered a distinct heir from the moment of live birth, even if death follows immediately. This ruling underscores the importance of physical signs of life in determining legal personhood and inheritance distribution within the family structure.
